title: Chocolate and walnut baklava
subtitle: filo pastry layered with chocolate and walnut filling, soaked in a honey syrup
excerpt: Chocolate and walnut baklava is made from layers of buttered filo pastry alternating with a filling of chopped walnuts and dark chocolate, baked until golden and immediately soaked in a honey and lemon syrup. The syrup is poured over the hot baklava and absorbed as it cools, giving the finished pastry its characteristic sticky, rich sweetness.
sourceNotes: Baklava is a pastry with deep roots in Ottoman and Middle Eastern cooking, with versions found across Turkey, Greece, Lebanon, Syria, and surrounding regions. The oldest known recipes date to the fifteenth century in Ottoman kitchens. The traditional nut used varies by region; walnuts dominate in Turkish and Greek versions. Dark chocolate is a contemporary addition not traditional to any particular region.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps at room temperature in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks. The flavour improves after 24 hours as the syrup soaks in fully.

content.text: Chocolate and walnut baklava is filo pastry layered with chopped walnuts and dark chocolate, buttered between each sheet, then baked until golden and crisp all the way through. The syrup goes on hot: pour cold syrup straight over the baklava as it comes out of the oven. This lets the pastry soak up the liquid without going soft.

items.prepNote: 1 packet, trimmed to fit the tin

content.text: Heat the oven to 160 degrees C (fan 140 degrees C / gas 3). Butter a 20 x 30 cm baking tin. Trim the filo sheets to fit the tin and keep covered with a damp cloth.
Mix the walnuts, chopped chocolate, cinnamon, and 2 tablespoons of caster sugar together in a bowl.

Layer 6 sheets of filo in the tin, brushing each generously with melted butter as you go. Spread half the nut and chocolate filling over the top in an even layer. Add 4 more sheets of filo, each brushed with butter. Spread the remaining filling. Finish with the remaining filo sheets, buttering each one.
Using a sharp knife, cut the baklava all the way through into diamond or square shapes. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the top is deep golden and the pastry is crisp throughout.

While the baklava bakes, make the syrup: put the caster sugar, water, honey, and lemon juice in a small saucepan. Stir over low heat until the sugar dissolves, then bring to the boil and simmer for 10 minutes. Leave to cool completely.

The moment the baklava comes out of the oven, pour the cold syrup evenly over the hot pastry. The hissing and bubbling is normal. Leave to soak and cool at room temperature for at least 2 hours before serving.

attrs.avoid: Avoid exposing the filo to air for too long; it becomes brittle within minutes.
attrs.fix: Keep the stack covered with a damp cloth and only uncover one sheet at a time. Torn sheets are not a problem in baklava; just overlap the tear with the next sheet.

attrs.problem: Baklava soggy rather than sticky and crisp
attrs.avoid: Avoid pouring warm syrup over warm baklava; the result is soggy pastry.
attrs.fix: The syrup must be cold when it meets the hot baklava. Make the syrup first and refrigerate it, or make it early so it has time to cool fully.
